turns.content: Start with 1^2,2^2,...,10^2. A morph replaces two entries a,b by a+1,b-1 only when a+1<b-1. Which sorted arithmetic progressions could be final multisets, given the preserved sum and the requirements of positive integer entries?

For sorted multisets X=(x_i) and Y=(y_i), define rho(X,X)=sum_i |x_i-y_i|. How much can one legal morph reduce the distance to a fixed sorted target Y? Prove a bound allowing the entries to be sorted again after the morph.
Calculate that distance from the sorted target sequence (1,4,9,16,25,36,49,64,81,100) to each candidate progression. Rank the candidates and obtain a lower bound on the number of morphs.
For a route to the nearest candidate, identify which entries must donate units and which must receive them. What must be checked at each transfer to ensure the morph remains legal?

Construct a route to the nearest progression that attains the lower bound. You may group transfers as "i to j; k", meaning k consecutive morphs that decrease the current entry at original index i and increase the entry at original index j. Original index i identifies the initial term i^2. Verify the legality of each block.
Combine the lower bound with the legal construction to give the least number of morphs needed.
